===== easyeda blocks --help (exit=0) =====
Query the standard circuit-block library — proven peripheral subcircuits
(CH340 USB-serial, ESP32 auto-download, XL1509 buck, SP3485 RS-485, CC1101 RF,
microSD…) whose internal topology is fixed and can be copied verbatim; only the
boundary nets (ports) get rebound to the host design.

The library is EMBEDDED in the binary, so these commands need no daemon, no open
EasyEDA window, and no skill files — a bare 'easyeda' install can look blocks up.

Usage:
  easyeda blocks [flags]
  easyeda blocks [command]

Available Commands:
  ls          List blocks (optionally filter by --category / --ready / --draft)
  search      Find blocks by id/desc/category/port/part (case-insensitive)
  show        Print a block's full JSON (parts, internal_nets, ports, notes)

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for blocks

Global Flags:
      --doc string                pin every mutating action to this schematic page / PCB (uuid or name): the CLI switches to it and confirms via live document.current before editing, refusing rather than land the edit on whatever page is foreground — removes the doc-switch race
      --force-stale-read string   deprecated compatibility option; stale PCB reads now continue with staleRisk and authoritative workflows still save, reload, then read back
      --host string               daemon host (default "127.0.0.1")
      --ports string              daemon port range (start-end) (default "60832-60841")
      --project string            route by project name/uuid instead of --window (survives windowId churn)
      --skip-version-check        deprecated compatibility option; version differences are diagnostic and no longer block actions

Use "easyeda blocks [command] --help" for more information about a command.
